title: Non-deterministic kernel-probing jitter causing intermittent p95/throughput regressions
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Summary: During a capacity burst on Feb 19 we observed intermittent large p95 and sustained throughput variability across the hosted API. Root cause traces to a recently-deployed scheduler probing heuristic that performs randomized kernel probing under load. Probing introduced kernel selection jitter and repeated small-batch kernel switches which caused KV cache churn, attention kernel warmup regressions, and an eviction storm on multi-tenant hosts. The behavior is non-deterministic (probabilistic probing) and manifests only under a narrow mix of short and long sequences with concurrent small-batch traffic. Impact: user-facing latency spikes (p95 up to ~420ms vs baseline ~75-120ms), tail amplification for some customers on Dedicated pools, and 8-12% effective throughput loss on affected hosts for ~45 minutes. This ticket tracks remediation, mitigation, telemetry, and rollout plans.

2026-02-19 23:10 UTC - Root cause narrowed: correlation with scheduler probing flag shipping in runtime-1.22 canary
2026-02-20 01:05 UTC - Emergency rollback of probing heuristic on canary hosts; p95 stabilized after rollback
2026-02-20 04:00 UTC - All canaries reverted; mitigation applied to affected Dedicated pools via feature-flag disable
2026-02-21 10:00 UTC - Full postmortem working group convened; hypothesis validated via deterministic replay
2026-02-27 16:00 UTC - Prototype deterministic-probing patch submitted (PR #8421) and bench-tested
2026-03-03 09:30 UTC - Additional telemetry dashboards added and synthetic canary workload created for regression detection
detection: Outage detected by automatic SLO alerting dashboards (p95 and token throughput deviation). Pager duty page triggered. Engineers used request traces and scheduler logs to identify increased kernel probing events correlated with high eviction counts and repeated kernel switches.
mitigation: Immediate: feature-flagged probing disabled on canary and rollout pools (rollback performed)
Short-term: revert probing heuristic in runtime-1.22 branch for next patch release
Medium-term: implement deterministic probing window and backoff to avoid frequent kernel flips
Long-term: extend KV cache telemetry to expose per-kernel miss-rate and add eviction-rate SLA tracking

ENG-81234-A3: Create synthetic mixed-sequence canary workload and add to CI gating for scheduler/runtime PRs (owner: Ben O9Connor, estimate: 2)
ENG-81234-A4: Update rollout playbook to include immediate single-host rollback and automated traffic draining (owner: SRE team, estimate: 2)
